# matterbridge_plugin (Resource)

A Matterbridge plugin. If Matterbridge does not have the plugin, the provider installs it with npm, adds it and restarts Matterbridge. A change to version installs that version (also an older version) and restarts Matterbridge. A change to the config saves the config and restarts Matterbridge or the plugin (see restart). If you destroy the resource, the plugin does not change, unless remove_on_destroy is true.

## Example Usage

```terraform
locals {
  # The devices to expose to Matter, with the features to hide for each device.
  matter_devices = {
    "Office Ceiling"        = []
    "Hallway Motion Sensor" = ["illuminance", "device_temperature"]
  }
}

resource "matterbridge_plugin" "zigbee2mqtt" {
  name    = "matterbridge-zigbee2mqtt"
  version = "3.3.0"
  config = {
    host                   = "mqtt://localhost"
    port                   = 1883
    username               = "matterbridge"
    topic                  = "zigbee2mqtt"
    whiteList              = keys(local.matter_devices)
    deviceFeatureBlackList = { for name, features in local.matter_devices : name => features if length(features) > 0 }
  }
  sensitive_config = { password = var.mqtt_password }
}

resource "matterbridge_plugin" "hass" {
  name             = "matterbridge-hass"
  version          = "1.6.0"
  config           = { host = "ws://homeassistant.local:8123", filterByLabel = "matter" }
  sensitive_config = { token = var.home_assistant_token }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The npm package, for example matterbridge-zigbee2mqtt. If you change it, OpenTofu replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `config` (Dynamic) The plugin config (configJson) as an object, for example { topic = "zigbee2mqtt", whiteList = ["Kitchen"] }. The provider manages only the top-level keys in this object. It compares each value as a whole, also lists and objects. Other keys do not change. If you remove a key, the provider stops managing it, and the value does not change. You cannot set name, type and version. Put secrets (password, token, and other settings that the plugin shows as passwords) in sensitive_config.
- `enabled` (Boolean) If false, the plugin and its devices stop. The default is true.
- `remove_on_destroy` (Boolean) If true, destroy removes the plugin from Matterbridge and uninstalls the npm package. Apply a change to this flag before you destroy the resource.
- `restart` (String) What the apply restarts after a config change: auto (the default: matterbridge in bridge mode, plugin in childbridge mode), plugin (only this plugin restarts, and the other plugins continue), matterbridge (all of Matterbridge), or none (the config applies at the next restart). In bridge mode, Matterbridge 3.11 does not register the devices again after a plugin restart. Thus, if the plugin has no devices after the restart, the provider restarts Matterbridge.
- `sensitive_config` (Map of String, Sensitive) More config keys with string values, as for config, but OpenTofu does not show the values. For example { password = var.mqtt_password }. A key cannot be in config and in sensitive_config. (It is a map of strings and not dynamic, because OpenTofu writes dynamic values to its debug log.)
- `version` (String) The npm version, for example 3.3.0. If it is different from the installed version, the apply installs it and restarts Matterbridge. If you do not set it, the provider does not change the version, and the attribute shows the installed version.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The plugin name.
- `latest_version` (String) The latest version on npm, as Matterbridge shows it.
- `registered_devices` (Number) The number of devices that the plugin registered in Matterbridge.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
tofu import matterbridge_plugin.zigbee2mqtt matterbridge-zigbee2mqtt
```
